claims.harm: Users unlikely to use multiple shells cannot toggle completion installation per shell individually
claims.quote: Users are at least somewhat unlikely to use multiple shells, so it probably makes sense to have a separate option for each one
claims.settled_by_quote: I also split the install option into INSTALL_BASH_COMPLETIONS and INSTALL_FISH_COMPLETIONS, both enabled by default.

claims.harm: Adding a completion file after configuration will not trigger reconfiguration or installation without manual cmake rerun, leading to flakiness
claims.quote: if(EXISTS ${...}): The problem is that adding a file may change the behavior of install, but only after cmake was manually rerun. Adding the file will not trigger the reconfiguration by itself.
claims.settled_by_quote: I replaced the if(EXISTS) checks with explicit HAS_BASH_COMPLETION and HAS_FISH_COMPLETION keywords.

claims.harm: Build options for completions don't affect build and 1:1 target-to-component relationship is inflexible; wrapper install_binary_component attracts responsibilities
claims.quote: The whole install_binary_component command should be inlined at the call sites and then removed.
claims.settled_by_quote: Many large projects, such as LLVM and Qt, use convenience wrappers extensively. In my opinion, they improve code maintainability as well
